author: Matt Rawlings
title: Assistant volleyball coach at Oregon high school sent 'explicit' messages to player, officials say - NewsBreak
text:
By Matt Rawlings ,
1 days ago
PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) A former volunteer assistant volleyball coach at Lebanon High School was arrested last month for “inappropriate” electronic messages to one of her players, Lebanon officials said.
Alyssa Baker was indicted by a grand jury in February on one count of luring a minor. She was lodged in the Linn County jail.
Officials say on Oct. 31, 2025, the victim’s parents contacted Lebanon police after discovering the “explicit” electronic messages sent to their daughter.
According to investigators, Baker had previously volunteered as the victim’s volleyball coach — the season had ended before the investigation had begun.
Baker’s volunteer status was terminated by the Lebanon Community School District.
The investigation is ongoing. The school district says they sent out the following message to Lebanon families on Tuesday.
“Late last year, a Lebanon Community School District volunteer volleyball coach had credentials revoked after the district received a report regarding inappropriate electronic communication with a student. This information was immediately relayed to our School Resource Officer and the Lebanon Police Department. The volunteer is no longer associated with the district.
All school district employees, contractors, and volunteers are mandatory reporters, meaning they are legally required to report any suspected child abuse within 24 hours of suspicion or receiving a report. Anyone who suspects child abuse or neglect should contact 855-503-SAFE (7233) or the Lebanon Police Department at (541) 451-1751.
Student safety remains our top priority. We recognize that situations like this may impact students in different ways, and staff are available to support any student who may need assistance. LCSD remains committed to providing a safe learning environment for all students.”
